significance.assessment: material but not yet demonstrated as a rolling-deployment protocol problem

reasoning.statement: MPDA reports that a V2X-ViT pipeline which performs explicit spatial resizing and channel truncation can complete heterogeneous inference while AP@0.7 falls from 71.2 in the homogeneous setting to 26.7 and 34.5 in two heterogeneous settings; the corresponding no-fusion values are 40.2 and 40.2, so one heterogeneous fusion case is materially worse than ego-only rather than merely crashing.

reasoning.statement: The pinned MPDA implementation makes heterogeneous tensors shape-compatible with bilinear interpolation to the ego spatial dimensions and channel truncation before concatenation and fusion. No model, codec, feature-schema, frame, time-semantics, or calibration capability is checked on this path.

A receiver can therefore accept a decodable, correctly shaped intermediate representation while collaboration harms task utility. This establishes the importance of compatibility control, but the public evidence is an offline heterogeneous-model experiment rather than a real over-the-air rolling upgrade.

exactClaimUnderReview.claim: During mixed-vendor or mixed-version cooperative-perception rollout, intermediate features, sparse queries, codebook indices, or occupancy summaries require a machine-checkable semantic wire capability contract covering task, coordinate frame, time semantics, codec and codebook identity, model family, calibration epoch, feature semantics, and safe degradation. Peers should negotiate a compatible exchange mode and fall back to raw, object-level, or ego-only operation when the offered representation is not compatible.
exactClaimUnderReview.excludedBroadClaim: The claim is not that messages generally need version numbers, hashes, or schema evolution.
exactClaimUnderReview.requiredEmpiricalCore: At least one real public cooperative-perception path must remain shape-decodable and execute without an exception while a cross-version or cross-configuration pairing causes semantic task degradation; a contract-driven reject or fallback control must prevent that degradation.

paths.finding: Serializes each collaborating feature as a bare NumPy arr_0 in timestamp.npz and preserves dataset YAML separately; the serialized feature has no producer model, config digest, codec, codebook, frame, calibration epoch, or feature-semantic identifier.
Loads npz.f.arr_0 without validating producer or semantic metadata.
Selects static source and target feature directories, pads arrays to maximum dimensions, and records only C/H/W in feature_mask; it does not carry or negotiate semantic capabilities.
Resizes collaborator features to ego H/W, truncates collaborator channels to the ego channel count, and then concatenates and fuses them. This is a concrete shape-compatible acceptance path.

capabilityCoverage.coordinateFrame: geometric transforms exist elsewhere in the dataset, but no producer capability assertion is bound to the feature blob
capabilityCoverage.timeSemantics: timestamp is used as a filename/key, not as a negotiated semantic contract

paths.finding: Builds encoders, backbones, aligners, and fusion from a static modality list in local configuration; runtime data carries agent_modality_list, after which aligned features are stacked and fused. No wire capability manifest is checked.
Maps modality labels from static configuration; unmatched_modality only tests whether a label belongs to the configured modality list.
Drops out-of-range or unknown-modality agents. This is a static filtering behavior, not negotiation among raw, object-level, intermediate, and ego-only modes.

The project warns that a released SECOND checkpoint has faulty input channels; spconv 2 detects the mismatch while spconv 1 lacks the sanity check and may produce degraded but superficially reasonable results. This is natural version-sensitive silent-error evidence, but it is not a V2X wire mismatch.

capabilityCoverage.coordinateFrame: pairwise transforms are supplied, but no feature-to-frame capability binding is checked
capabilityCoverage.featureSemantics: modality label and configured aligner, not a versioned schema/hash
capabilityCoverage.safeFallbackNegotiation: unknown modalities can be dropped; no peer handshake or tier selection

paths.finding: Constructs per-modality encoders, adapters, reverters, fusion, and heads from static configuration. Runtime agent modality labels are filtered against that list; accepted features pass through configured learned mappings, are stacked, and are fused without checking a producer model/config hash, codec/codebook identity, calibration epoch, or feature schema.
Declares modality mappings and a protocol model statically; it is not an exchanged or authenticated runtime capability contract.
States that checkpoints are being prepared for release, preventing a complete official-checkpoint replay at this revision.

naturalOrPublishedFailure.configuration: Hetero1 uses different PointPillar configurations and an unseen test model; Hetero2 pairs a PointPillar ego model with a distinct SECOND collaborator. The paper's naive baseline applies spatial interpolation and channel dropping so fusion executes.
naturalOrPublishedFailure.result: For AP@0.7, V2X-ViT reports 71.2 in the homogeneous condition, 26.7 in Hetero1, and 34.5 in Hetero2. No Fusion reports 40.2, including the heterogeneous columns; Late Fusion reports 51.7 and 52.8 in Hetero1 and Hetero2. Thus Hetero1 is a verified silent harmful-fusion case rather than a shape exception.

explicitRejectOrFallbackControl.requiredControl: Wrap the real MPDA feature blob in a deterministic capability envelope; reject a mismatched feature-schema/codebook/calibration contract before tensor fusion and rerun the exact sample as ego-only or object-level fusion.

verifiedNaturalOrConstructedFailure.boundary: The verified failure is a public cross-configuration offline evaluation. It does not yet prove a multi-vendor rolling deployment, packet-level negotiation, or calibration-epoch failure.

nearestPriorArt.overlap: Identifies heterogeneous model/config feature-domain gaps, constructs shape-compatible heterogeneous fusion, measures harmful degradation, and learns domain adaptation.
nearestPriorArt.difference: Does not expose a runtime semantic capability manifest or negotiate fail-closed exchange tiers.

nearestPriorArt.overlap: Creates a unified feature space and backward alignment for newly introduced models/modalities; filters unknown static modality labels.
nearestPriorArt.difference: The inspected runtime path relies on local configuration and modality labels rather than an exchanged machine-checkable semantic contract or tier negotiation.

nearestPriorArt.overlap: Maps heterogeneous senders through adapters/reverters into a shared protocol domain and is explicitly task- and model-agnostic.
nearestPriorArt.difference: It is a learned representation protocol configured before inference, not verified runtime capability admission with raw/object/ego fallback.

nearestPriorArt.overlap: Negotiates a common representation and learns sender/receiver transformations across heterogeneous agents.
nearestPriorArt.difference: The inspected paper describes representation negotiation/training, not a deployment-time wire handshake over model, codec, frame, calibration, and fallback capabilities.

nearestPriorArt.overlap: Together provide standard type identity, type description, discovery, assignability, and consistency enforcement suitable for transporting a capability envelope.
nearestPriorArt.difference: They do not define learned-perception semantics or the automotive fallback policy; those remain application contracts.

elementByElementComparison.priorCoverage: MPDA directly covers it through interpolation/channel dropping and heterogeneous AP degradation; HEAL also documents a version-sensitive checkpoint issue that may silently degrade under spconv 1, though that issue is not a wire exchange.
elementByElementComparison.residue: No novelty remains in merely observing that equal/alignable tensor shapes can have incompatible learned meanings.

elementByElementComparison.priorCoverage: MPDA, HEAL, STAMP, PolyInter, MACP, CodeAlign, and NegoCollab already adapt heterogeneous feature domains or map them into common representations.
elementByElementComparison.residue: A generic adapter, distillation loss, shared latent space, or codebook translation is not novel enough for this candidate.

elementByElementComparison.priorCoverage: DDS-XTypes, ROS REP-2011, and Protobuf evolution rules already provide type identifiers, hashes/descriptions, assignability, and wire-safety rules.
elementByElementComparison.residue: The envelope serialization and ordinary version/hash negotiation are engineering reuse, not the research contribution.

elementByElementComparison.priorCoverage: ETSI CPM and SAE J3224 cover object-level time, position, sensor, and object semantics; audited neural feature paths implicitly rely on local model/config and geometric transforms.
elementByElementComparison.residue: A precise compatibility relation joining task, coordinate/time semantics, codec/codebook, model family, calibration epoch, and learned feature semantics was not found in the inspected cooperative-perception runtime paths.

elementByElementComparison.priorCoverage: Backward/forward-compatible representation learning covers generation compatibility by training; NVIDIA Dynamo isolates incompatible model generations operationally.
elementByElementComparison.residue: Per-link, deployment-time admission for V2X learned representations during partial fleet rollout remains unverified as prior art in this search.

elementByElementComparison.priorCoverage: Cooperative-perception papers evaluate no fusion and late/object-level fusion as baselines, and HEAL/STAMP can statically drop unsupported modalities. ETSI/SAE standardize object-level exchange.
elementByElementComparison.residue: A machine-driven handshake selecting the safest feasible tier from peer capabilities, with measured refusal errors and safety/utility outcomes, was not found.

elementByElementComparison.priorCoverage: The audited assets provide heterogeneous configurations and partial checkpoints, but not a verified old-version/new-version over-the-air rollout pair with contract and fallback.
elementByElementComparison.residue: This is the critical missing evidence and must be produced before a go decision.

noveltyResidue.retainedClaim: The potentially novel unit is an empirically derived, perception-specific compatibility relation enforced at runtime during mixed-generation deployment, coupled to negotiated fail-closed exchange tiers and evaluated on real public model/config pairs that otherwise execute silently and harm task utility.
notNovelEnough: adding a version or hash field
another common latent protocol or codebook
reporting only average AP without refusal and fallback behavior
noveltyResidue.unresolvedNoveltyRisk: NegoCollab, STAMP, HEAL, PolyInter, and CodeAlign substantially occupy learned compatibility. The proposal survives only if it is framed and validated as runtime operational safety/interoperability rather than representation alignment.

minimumExecutableStudy.objective: Demonstrate on fixed public checkpoints that legacy or shape-only admission silently accepts semantically incompatible representations, then test whether a semantic contract selects a safer public fallback without rejecting known-compatible peers.
prerequisiteGate: Pin dataset release, code commits, environment lock, and cryptographic hashes for every checkpoint/config/codebook/calibration artifact.

Obtain at least three independently trained public checkpoint pairs: one same-architecture configuration change, one architecture change such as PointPillar versus SECOND, and one adapter/codebook/protocol change.
Require the unmodified legacy fusion path to complete without exception for each claimed mismatch; shape crashes are logged but do not count as the target phenomenon.
Abort the study claim if only synthetic tensors can be executed or if official weights/features cannot be reproduced.
contractFields: coordinate frame convention and transform provenance
timestamp clock domain, reference instant, and freshness policy
producer model family and checkpoint/config digest
feature stage, stride, channel semantics, quantization, and normalization schema
sensor/calibration bundle digest and calibration epoch
declared compatible receiver families or adapter identifiers
supported fallback tiers and resource limits
protocol: Serialize the existing MPDA feature blob unchanged and bind it to a signed or integrity-protected manifest; do not encode semantics from the filename alone.
Replay the same scenario/checkpoint pair under legacy unchecked fusion, shape-only checking, model/config allowlisting, the full semantic contract, and an offline oracle compatibility matrix.

For an incompatible offer, select the highest predeclared mutually supported tier in order: verified intermediate representation, raw sensor data only when the receiver has the exact decoder and bandwidth budget, ETSI/SAE-style object-level exchange, then ego-only.
Measure the decision before decoding/fusion, the chosen tier, end-to-end task utility, harmful-collaboration events, bytes, latency, and rejection reason.
Repeat on HEAL only after public checkpoint/config hashes and the pinned legacy-spconv environment are reproducible; add STAMP only after official checkpoints are available.

failure dossier containing examples that ran without exception yet harmed task utility

independentUnits.minimumDiversity: At least three checkpoint pairs spanning same-family config change, cross-architecture change, and adapter/codebook/protocol change, with multiple routes/scenarios per pair.

successCriteria.criterion: At least two non-synthetic public producer/receiver pairs complete the legacy intermediate-fusion path without an exception and show a reproducible task regression relative to ego-only on paired scenarios.
successCriteria.why: This is the minimum evidence that the problem is semantic and operational rather than a shape crash.

successCriteria.criterion: The full contract rejects every deliberately incompatible manifest before fusion and accepts all audited known-compatible manifests, with each decision traceable to a declared field or registered adapter relation.
successCriteria.why: Machine checkability requires deterministic admission behavior, not a post-hoc anomaly score.

successCriteria.criterion: For rejected pairs, negotiated fallback is never worse than ego-only on the preregistered primary task metric and reports its latency and bandwidth cost.
successCriteria.why: A compatibility detector without a safe operational response does not satisfy the candidate claim.

successCriteria.criterion: The full semantic contract prevents failures that a shape-only gate and a producer-model/config allowlist both miss, including at least one frame/time/calibration or codebook/feature-schema case grounded in a real public stack.
successCriteria.why: Otherwise the rich contract has no demonstrated value over existing schema/version practice.

successCriteria.criterion: Results persist across scenario clusters and more than one checkpoint pair; no conclusion is based solely on synthetic channel permutation.
successCriteria.why: The unit of evidence is a deployment pairing, not a tensor perturbation.

killCriteria: No fixed public checkpoint pair can reproduce shape-compatible, exception-free degradation after the documented environment and data are restored.
All observed failures are tensor shape/type crashes or deliberately synthetic perturbations.
A model/config hash allowlist prevents the same failures with the same acceptance and fallback utility as the richer semantic contract.
HEAL, STAMP, NegoCollab, CodeAlign, or a V2X standard is found to already expose an equivalent deployment-time capability relation and negotiated tier fallback in released code/specification.
The proposed fields cannot predict empirical compatibility without running task data, making the contract only a renamed offline compatibility matrix.
Fallback selection causes task utility below ego-only, violates the declared latency/bandwidth envelope, or silently changes task/frame/time semantics.
Official assets needed for at least two independent real pairs remain unavailable or legally/non-technically unreproducible.
The study evaluates only average AP and cannot identify harmful-collaboration events, refusal errors, or the exact admission reason.

risks.detail: HEAL, STAMP, MPDA, NegoCollab, PolyInter, MACP, and CodeAlign already cover much of heterogeneous representation adaptation.
risks.mitigation: Restrict the claim to runtime admission and tier negotiation, and compare against their learned compatibility mechanisms.

risks.detail: DDS-XTypes, ROS type hashes/descriptions, Protobuf evolution, and rolling-generation isolation cover the generic protocol machinery.
risks.mitigation: Treat them as implementation substrate and require empirical proof that perception-specific semantic fields add value beyond hashes and schemas.

risks.detail: STAMP checkpoints were not released at the pinned revision; CodeFilling has no code at its pinned revision; CodeAlign code was forthcoming; MPDA's immediate full replay assets were not verified.
risks.mitigation: Make asset preflight a kill gate and publish checksums and exact setup before experimentation.

risks.detail: MPDA proves offline heterogeneous feature failure, not packet loss, asynchronous clocks, adversarial manifests, or real fleet rollout behavior.
risks.mitigation: Do not claim deployment safety until the contract is exercised at an actual serialization boundary with timing and fallback telemetry.

risks.detail: A producer can declare the wrong model, frame, calibration, or codebook; a manifest alone is not semantic correctness.
risks.mitigation: Bind digests to artifacts, authenticate provenance where the threat model requires it, and retain runtime plausibility/safety monitors as a separate layer.

risks.detail: Different model hashes can be compatible through a registered adapter, while identical families can be incompatible after preprocessing or calibration changes.
risks.mitigation: Represent compatibility as a receiver-specific relation over declared artifacts and adapters, not equality of one version field.

risks.detail: Raw fallback may exceed bandwidth or require an unavailable decoder; object-level fallback can use a different ontology; ego-only reduces coverage.
risks.mitigation: Negotiate only predeclared feasible tiers and evaluate each tier's utility, latency, bandwidth, and ontology mapping.

verdictRationale: The problem is real enough to continue: MPDA supplies primary, task-level evidence that shape-aligned heterogeneous fusion can execute and underperform ego-only, and the pinned code shows exactly how dimensions are forced to match without semantic metadata.

The broad novelty claim does not survive. Learned heterogeneous alignment/common protocols are already crowded by MPDA, HEAL, STAMP, NegoCollab, PolyInter, MACP, and CodeAlign, while generic type/schema negotiation is established by DDS-XTypes, ROS REP-2011, and Protobuf.

The remaining contribution is narrower: runtime, perception-specific admission plus negotiated safe fallback during a mixed-generation rollout, with evidence that richer semantics outperform a simple model/config allowlist.

A go decision is not justified because this audit did not execute a complete public old/new checkpoint pair or a contract-driven reject/fallback control. Several closest public assets are incomplete or environment-sensitive.
The next artifact should be the minimum executable measurement study, not a new learned alignment architecture or a general message-version proposal.
evidenceLimitations: No other reviewer output or existing idea-audit file was read, preserving independence but preventing comparison with parallel reviews.
The strongest failure evidence is MPDA's published offline cross-configuration benchmark, not a live multi-vendor rolling deployment.
The local forward probe was not completed, so no locally generated metric or explicit reject/fallback result is claimed.
Absence findings are bounded to the listed files and commits; they do not prove that metadata is absent from every branch, fork, unpublished deployment wrapper, or later release.
HEAL's spconv/checkpoint warning is a natural silent-error analogue inside a model stack, not evidence of a network semantic-wire mismatch.
STAMP checkpoints, CodeFilling implementation, and CodeAlign implementation were unavailable at the audited revisions, limiting executable comparison with the nearest learned protocols.
ETSI and SAE findings concern published object-level interfaces; this audit does not claim that every current draft, profile, or proprietary extension omits neural-feature capabilities.
Search breadth was substantial but stopped at the user's direction on 2026-07-31; the verdict is therefore revise rather than a claim of exhaustive global novelty.
